verdict.rationale: Dagster's own docs say you can use its UI or APIs to run subsets of dbt models, which covers re-running a single table without rebuilding everything. Its asset model, including Fivetran and dlt connectors represented as individual assets, implies per-table materialization. Partitions appear only in a changelog note about wiping dynamic partitions, and nothing documents backfilling history. Missing for 10: explicit backfill/partition-range re-run documentation, documented single-asset resync for Fivetran/Airbyte/dlt syncs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can backfill history or resync a single table without rebuilding the whole pipeline

citations.quote: Use Dagster's UI or APIs to run subsets of your dbt models, seeds, and snapshots.
The dagster-fivetran library provides a FivetranAccountComponent which can be used to easily represent Fivetran connectors as assets in Dagster.
